Question ID: STAT_U03_L07_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.BVM.8

What is 18/60 as a percent?

answer.text: 30 percent

feedback.text: 18 divided by 60 equals 0.30, or 30 percent.

answer.text: 18 percent

feedback.text: This uses the part as the percent instead of dividing by the total.

answer.text: 60 percent

feedback.text: This uses the total as the percent instead of comparing part to whole.

answer.text: 78 percent

feedback.text: This adds the values instead of dividing.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U03_L07_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.BVM.9

Which statement describes a conditional relative frequency?

answer.text: A count divided by its row or column total

feedback.text: Conditional relative frequency uses a specific condition as the total.

answer.text: A count inside a table divided by the grand total

feedback.text: That is a joint relative frequency.

answer.text: A row total divided by a column total

feedback.text: This mixes two margins and does not define conditional relative frequency.

answer.text: The title of a two-way table

feedback.text: A title is not a frequency.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U03_L07_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.BVM.10

Group A has 16 of 40 students choose tutoring. What percent is that?

answer.text: 24 percent

feedback.text: This subtracts 16 from 40 instead of dividing.

answer.text: 40 percent
30 percent

feedback.text: This is not 16 divided by 40.

answer.text: 56 percent

feedback.text: This adds 16 and 40.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U03_L07_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.BVM.9

Why are conditional percentages useful when group sizes differ?

answer.text: They prove causation

feedback.text: Percentages support comparison but do not prove cause.

answer.text: They compare each group using its own total

feedback.text: This gives a fairer comparison across different group sizes.

answer.text: They remove the need for context

feedback.text: Context is still needed to interpret the data.

answer.text: They make raw counts larger

feedback.text: Percentages do not change counts.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U03_L07_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.BVM.10

Group A has 18 of 45 choose tutoring and Group B has 30 of 75 choose tutoring. Which conclusion is best?

answer.text: Group B is higher because 30 is greater than 18

feedback.text: This uses raw counts and ignores that Group B is larger.

answer.text: Group A is higher because 45 is smaller than 75

feedback.text: The denominator alone does not decide the percentage.

answer.text: Both groups have the same conditional percentage

feedback.text: 18/45 and 30/75 both equal 40 percent.

answer.text: The data prove tutoring caused group membership

feedback.text: A two-way table does not prove causation.
